messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — noticed a small window where raw request bodies are visible in the metrics heatmap before redaction runs. Might be ~8-12s depending on backlog. Is that expected?
Devin Patel: ugh. which heatmap? the per-route telemetry one in Console?
Maria Chen: yes. the realtime request/response volume heatmap. It looks like we store the full payload in the in-memory shard until the redaction job picks it up.
Samir Ortiz: That's the debounce behavior we added to avoid thrashing on high-qps routes. We batch redaction jobs every 10s by default.
Zara K.: That was intentional to avoid CPU spikes, but we probably shouldn't keep unredacted payloads in memory. We could swap to a pointer to disk-encrypted temp and run redaction from there.
Devin Patel: Alternatives: 1) reduce debounce to 2s for routes flagged as "sensitive"; 2) stream-redact inline (sync path) for high-risk tenants; 3) encrypt-and-evict to disk asap then redact.
Maria Chen: For auditability, security wants both: minimal exposure window + an ops-visible flag for canary redaction changes.
Samir Ortiz: quick config idea: 
```
redaction: {
  mode: "async-batch",
  debounce_ms: 10000,
  sensitive_overrides: {
    "tenant_*": { debounce_ms: 2000, sync_redact: true }
  },
  temp_store: "encrypted-ssd",
  inspect_when_unredacted: false
}
```
Zara K.: If we do 'inspect_when_unredacted: true' that lets ops replay raw for X minutes — security will object unless it's opt-in and audited.
Devin Patel: Also noticed the telemetry heatmap aggregates by time-bucket; that aggregation currently pulls raw payload meta before redaction. Suggest we switch to storing only hashed route/signature + sized bucket, no raw keys.
Maria Chen: Agreed. We should add a routing policy rule to tag sensitive routes early so the ingestion pipeline knows to use stricter pipeline. Something like route.metadata.sensitivity = high.
Samir Ortiz: Implementation notes: changing debounce for sensitive routes is easy; the hard part is making sure prior-in-flight buffers are flushed/evicted during rollout. Rollout plan: start with a canary group of 3 tenants, enable reduced debounce + encrypted temp store, monitor latency/cpu and heatmap missing data.
Zara K.: UX for Console: in addition to the heatmap color, add a tiny badge for "raw-suppressed" with hover text: why and when. That helps SREs and PMs not assume missing data = bug.
Maria Chen: Good call. Also add a per-tenant audit checkbox: "allow temporary unredacted inspection" with TTL and require manual approval + audit log entry.
Devin Patel: infra-bot just reported a small deploy note: 
infra-bot: deploy/rolling redaction-worker v2 -> staging started at 2865002000. watch: /alerts/redaction-latency > 5s
Samir Ortiz: For rollout we also need migration path for metrics backfill: heatmap that lost raw labels should have a marker so analysts know values are partial.
Zara K.: Can product accept reduced granularity for sensitive tenants? Product needs visibility but maybe aggregated counts and token-length distributions are enough.
Maria Chen: I'll draft a short RFC: goals: remove in-memory unredacted payload retention; per-route sensitivity overrides; console UX for suppressed raw data; audited opt-in inspection with TTL. Will include proposed canary tenants + telemetry gating.
Devin Patel: TL;DR: change debounce defaults, temp-store encryption, route tagging, and console badges. I'll prototype the reduced debounce config and a small benchmark.
Samir Ortiz: I'll add a migration script to mark existing heatmap buckets as 'partial' for the time range we flip the pipeline.
Zara K.: Ping me when RFC is ready. I'll scope Console work and the badge copy.
Maria Chen: Thanks. cc @infra-bot for deploy watch. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: monitor/redaction-latency: current=2.1s, p95=4.7s, queue_depth=120
